subject: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): scope, design partners, and resourcing ask

body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Victor Alvarez <victor@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): scope, design partners, and resourcing ask

Hi Irene + Markus,

I want to lock the alpha scope for the "VPC Terraform modules" effort and align on (a) who we target as design partners and (b) what we’re committing to ship, so we can staff it cleanly.

What we’re trying to solve (repeatable pain in discovery/pilots): customer VPC variability + networking gaps cause week-long stalls (endpoints/DNS/NAT/SG boundaries/log sinks). The goal is to publish Redwood-validated Terraform modules that encode safe defaults for a standard Private footprint.

Proposed alpha deliverables (AWS-only, VPC foundation):
- VPC + subnet layout (public/private), routing + NAT strategy
- Security group patterns (cluster, LB, egress)
- VPC endpoints module (ECR api+dkr, S3, STS, CW Logs, etc.) + private DNS behavior options
- Logging defaults (Flow Logs to CloudWatch or S3) + sane retention defaults
- IAM scaffolding (installer execution role + permission boundary pattern)
- CI: fmt/validate + tflint + checkov (or equivalent) + integration test harness w/ ephemeral env
- Examples + docs (reference architecture + deployment guide + supported topologies/extension points)

Non-goals for alpha:
- multi-cloud
- end-to-end cluster/app install (installer/Helm handles)
- bespoke enterprise topology support beyond documented extension points

Draft timeline (assuming we start next week):
- Jun 10–Jun 28: discovery/requirements + supported topology matrix
- Jul 1–Jul 12: design + ADRs (module boundaries + interface, validation/testing)
- Jul 15–Aug 23: implementation + CI + examples
- Aug 26–Sep 20: dogfood + 1–2 design partner pilots
- Target alpha tag/release: week of Sep 23

Design partner candidates (top of funnel):
- Acme Bank (regulated; heavy endpoint/logging/least-privilege asks)
- Northstar Healthcare (strict egress controls; wants VPC-first POC)

Resourcing ask:
1) Infra Eng: can we commit an owner (Victor?) + 1 implementer (Bruno?) for 6–8 weeks for the module build/CI? Nina for topology constraints review as-needed.
2) SE/ProServ: Markus, can you commit a point person (you or Colin) for design partner selection + weekly feedback loop + pilot comms?
3) Security review: Naomi/Marcus will review logging + IAM boundary approach, but I want to make sure we aren’t creating a new dependency chain that slows us down.

Attachments:
- VPC-Terraform-Alpha-Scope-v0.3.pdf
- Design-Partner-Candidate-List_20250605.xlsx

If this seems directionally right, I’ll update the PRD draft + kick off the Linear epic (ENG-4821 / PM-913) with owners.

Thanks,
Vivek

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference



From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, Victor Alvarez <victor@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): scope, design partners, and resourcing ask

This matches what we’ve been hearing from support + pilots.

On resourcing: I can commit Victor as technical owner for the module interfaces + defaults. Bruno can implement, but I need to confirm he’s done with the current runtime infra sprint by 6/14.

Two notes:
1) Integration tests: please don’t run full ephemeral bringup on every PR by default. We can do fmt/validate/tflint/checkov per-PR; ephemeral apply/destroy nightly + on release branches.
2) NAT strategy: we need to be explicit on the AZ assumptions. We got burned recently by customers with 2-AZ VPCs + differing subnet maps. Defaults must be safe and the module should validate mismatches early.

If you’re good with that, Victor can start an interface doc next week and we’ll align in #eng-infra.

-Irene



From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Victor Alvarez <victor@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 10:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): scope, design partners, and resourcing ask

+1.

Design partners:
- Acme Bank is the right "hard mode" tester. They’ve been clear they need: (a) endpoint-first (ECR/S3/STS), (b) audit logs to customer-owned sinks, (c) clear statement on public egress behavior.
- Northstar is good for the egress-restricted + healthcare compliance angle.

I can commit Colin O’Donnell as the weekly point person (I’ll stay in the loop for escalations). We should set expectations that alpha will have version pinning + limited topology support and that upgrades may require coordination.

Also: can we include an example tfvars for “tight egress” and “standard egress” so SE isn’t inventing variables per customer?

-Markus



From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Victor Alvarez <victor@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 11:11 AM PT
Subject: Re: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): scope, design partners, and resourcing ask

Great.

Re: tests — agreed on per-PR vs nightly. I’ll capture that explicitly as part of the validation/testing ADR so we don’t accidentally make CI unusable.

Re: NAT/AZ assumptions — yes. Let’s bake in:
- explicit variable for az_count / subnet mapping
- validation errors when private subnets < expected
- doc that “single NAT” is optional but not the default for prod

Markus: yes on example tfvars. I want at least:
- “baseline” (standard private footprint)
- “restricted egress” (no 0.0.0.0/0 from private subnets; endpoints required)
- “customer VPN/DX placeholder” (outputs/hooks without hardcoding their network)

Next steps (proposed):
- Victor: draft module boundary + interface outline (inputs/outputs) by EOW next week
- Bruno: start repo skeleton + initial example env once interface doc is ready
- Colin (via Markus): confirm willingness from Acme + Northstar to be alpha design partners and that they can do weekly check-ins
- Naomi: quick sanity pass on logging + IAM boundary language we’ll put in docs (alpha posture statement)

Talia — can you help set up a 30-min kickoff early next week? I’ll drop a calendar hold once you confirm.

Vivek



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, Victor Alvarez <victor@redwoodinference.com>, Bruno Silva <bruno@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia@redwoodinference.com>, Nina Petrova <nina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 1:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): scope, design partners, and resourcing ask

Works for me.

Two guardrails I want captured in the alpha docs (so we don’t over-promise):
1) Logging defaults: flow logs on by default, but destination is customer-owned by default (either CW Logs in their account with retention set, or S3 bucket they own). Redwood should not be the default sink.
2) IAM: permission boundary pattern must be recommended and supported; installer role should be scoped and not include broad IAM:*.

If we publish a clear “secure-by-default posture” section, it will make the security review with Acme materially easier.

Naomi
